proposals.title: Proposal 1: One list sheet
proposals.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: a finished raster design proposal board for the Lists app of Inner Breeze. Draw a landscape 1536 x 1024 image containing exactly THREE large portrait phone UI screens side by side, equal size and vertically aligned, fully visible. Put the proposal title across the top and a short caption below each phone. Minimal dark backdrop, no extra phones, no perspective, no hands, no illustrations or charts. Large, crisp, correctly spelled English interface typography. This is a practical high-fidelity mobile UX design, not decorative concept art.

VISUAL SYSTEM: Inner Breeze dark navy background approximately #1b2838, slightly lighter slate-blue panels and rounded fields, pale off-white primary text, blue-gray secondary text, medium muted blue selected chips and primary controls, small red destructive actions. Restrained thin dividers, generous spacing, matte flat UI, soft corner radii. Avoid bright gradients or neon. Simple thin-line icons. All text must be readable at this board size. The page starts with wrapping list chips, with no title bar above them. Example chips: Shopping selected in filled blue, Home, Weekend, Groceries and a final "+" chip, wrapping to two rows. Chip rows contain ONLY list chips and the final plus, except the tiny selected-chip gear specifically required in proposal 4. No extra toolbar crammed onto chip rows.

PAGE CONTENT AND GESTURES: Keep the top "Add a task..." field and a separate blue "Add" button. Ordinary item rows contain only task text "Milk", "Bread", "Fresh fruit", with calm spacing and no checkbox, no pencil, no trash, no action buttons. Tap completes; swipe right edits; swipe left deletes and offers Undo. Crucially, in the LEFT phone, show "Fresh fruit" in an ACTIVE INLINE EDIT STATE: that exact row becomes a rounded text field with a visible text cursor and a small checkmark at its right edge to save. The active inline editor is the sole permitted row-control exception. Other item rows remain text only. The top field MUST still say "Add a task..." and the top button MUST still say "Add". Never move item editing to that top field. Finished items are hidden with pull-down reveal; do NOT add any finished/completed-items text or counter.

SHARING: Clear, specific people names on the list page: "Alice" and "Cedar (invited)", not generic collaborator counts. One coherent sharing entry per proposal. Sharing UI has exact rows with aligned circular initial avatars, "You" with noneditable "Owner", "Alice" with compact "Can edit", and "Cedar (invited)" with compact "Read only". Pending status must be explicit. For invitation, use "Add people" / "Invite by name", query "Da", and a visible compact autocomplete suggestion panel with "Dana" and "Daniel". Do not suggest Alice or Cedar because they already have access. No oversized dropdown boxes. Roles are exactly Owner, Can edit, Read only; compact chevrons or pills can open role choices. Preserve comfortable hit targets with visually small controls.

SAFETY: Delete list is available ONLY to the owner, who is the viewer in these mockups. Show a clear confirmation in the RIGHT phone with "Delete this list?", a short consequence "The list and its items will be permanently deleted.", and separate "Cancel" and red "Delete list" buttons. Never use "tap again" as confirmation. At board-caption level, label deletion "Owner only". Do not add implementation details to the product UI. All three phones depict the SAME proposal, not three alternative proposals.

PROPOSAL 1 — ONE LIST SHEET.
Exact top title: "Proposal 1: One list sheet".
The distinctive interaction: tap the already selected chip or long-press any list chip to open one combined bottom sheet for that list. The selected chip itself is the single management/sharing entry. There are NO separate Share, Edit, gear or overflow icons anywhere on the list page. Make this calm and understandable through the caption "Tap the selected chip to manage". Show a noninteractive, compact but clearly readable "Alice · Cedar (invited)" text line beneath the chips, then the Add field, then the text-only items with Fresh fruit editing inline.

LEFT PHONE: the list page as above. Do not open a popup or sheet here. Inline editing is prominent enough to see.
Caption: "Selected chip opens settings · Items edit in place".

MIDDLE PHONE: the list page dimly behind a tall bottom sheet with a drag handle. The sheet begins with a small label "List name" and a rounded editable field showing "Shopping", so rename happens in this same sheet. Next "People with access" and aligned avatar-name-role rows: You / Owner, Alice / Can edit with a tiny chevron, Cedar (invited) / Read only with a tiny chevron. Under them the Add people field with Da and Dana / Daniel suggestions, plus a compact Invite button. At the very bottom a quiet red "Delete list" text action. All fit comfortably without overlapping.
Caption: "Rename, access and invitations in one sheet".

RIGHT PHONE: the same combined list sheet with its name field actively editing "Groceries" and a small "Save name" action beside the field. Keep access rows recognizable. In the bottom danger section, show the explicit deletion confirmation card with consequence and Cancel / Delete list. It is a confirmation state, not an accidental second tap. Do not cover the name field with the confirmation.
Caption: "Rename in place · Confirm deletion · Owner only".

PROPOSAL 2 — PEOPLE FIRST.
Exact top title: "Proposal 2: People first".
The distinctive interaction: a slim access line directly below the wrapping chips shows two overlapping initial avatars A and C, followed by the readable names on two compact lines "Alice" and "Cedar (invited)". This entire avatar-and-names block is the single Share entry. At the far right of that SAME slim line is a quiet vertical three-dot menu for Rename and Delete list. No separate pencil or person-plus icon row. Keep the line slim with no redundant list title, no "With collaborators" text. Below are Add a task... / Add and text-only rows.

LEFT PHONE: show the people line as a subtle integrated header, then Add field and rows, Fresh fruit editing inline with its save check. Keep lots of navy negative space below.
Caption: "Tap the names to share · Swipe right to edit inline".

MIDDLE PHONE: a focused, polished Google Docs-style bottom Share sheet headed "Share Shopping", with a compact Done action at the top right. People with access has the aligned avatar rows You / Owner, Alice / Can edit chevron, Cedar (invited) / Read only chevron. Below a field "Invite by name" containing Da, suggestions Dana and Daniel, a compact invitation role control "Can edit" and Invite button. No list-name field or delete inside this Share sheet; those belong to the overflow flow.
Caption: "Names and small role labels, all aligned".

RIGHT PHONE: show the page's overflow menu anchored beneath the three-dot button, with "Rename" and red "Delete list". Below it show a compact "Rename list" form, editable name "Groceries", Cancel and Save. In the lower half show a distinct anchored confirmation card for the Delete flow: Delete this list?, consequence text, Cancel and red Delete list. Treat this phone as a clear compact management-state demonstration, with rename and the confirmation separated by space; no full settings page. Make the hierarchy legible and avoid overlapping cards.
Caption: "Overflow for rename and safe delete · Owner only".

PROPOSAL 3 — EDIT AT THE CHIP.
Exact top title: "Proposal 3: Edit at the chip".
The distinctive interaction: tapping the already-selected chip again turns ONLY that chip into an editable name, with a compact context popover immediately under it containing a person-plus icon and "Share", then a separated red "Delete list". There are no management icons in the resting chip row and no Share/Edit toolbar on the page. Sharing lives in that context popover. The page always has a simple noninteractive text line under the chips "Alice · Cedar (invited)" so the people are unmistakable. The tiny chip editor can commit by the keyboard Enter key, and dismissal cancels; do not cram save/delete/share controls inside the chip row.

LEFT PHONE: resting Shopping-selected list page, Alice · Cedar (invited) visible under the chips, Add a task... / Add below, Milk, Bread and Fresh fruit actively editing inline with a small save check. The list chips remain otherwise pristine.

Use clean, small ROLE PILLS at the far right of aligned people rows, not large dropdowns: You / Owner (quiet fixed text or pill without chevron), Alice / Can edit pill, Cedar (invited) / Read only pill. Below is Add people field containing Da, with suggestions Dana and Daniel in a slim suggestion card, and an Invite action. A small helper outside the phone may say "Tap a role pill to change access"; do not put long guidance inside the interface.
Caption: "Compact sharing sheet with role pills".

RIGHT PHONE: the Shopping selected chip is now a rounded input containing "Groceries" and a visible caret. Its small context popover directly below has exactly Share and Delete list. Keep all other chips and final +. In the lower middle of this phone, a separate compact delete-confirmation card reads Delete this list?, consequence text, Cancel and red Delete list, triggered by the context action. Keep the editable chip and its popover visible above the confirmation. The top Add field remains Add a task..., never used for rename or item edit. Clear visual priority on editing at the location of the list name.
Caption: "Tap selected chip to rename · Safe delete · Owner only".
